fair_value_reason: NTM adjusted EPS at 2027-09-28 = 0.25 x FY27 consensus $9.16 + 0.75 x FY28 ~$11.00 (the $11.19 aggregator shaded for Goldman's +12% 2028 capex growth) = ~$10.54. At 24.5x (below ETN 26.8x and NVT 24.8x FY27, above the 22x AI-infra median) that is ~$258. Diluted shares ~393M. Horizon net cash ~+$0.3B after UIG (~$1/share), which is immaterial. The deposit-normalized FCF-yield legs ($240-255) cross-check within ~7%. This is $3 above the agents' mean of $255.2, mainly because I reverse agent_3's unsupported FY27 haircut.
supervisor_summary: VRT at $244 is 26.6x FY27 consensus ($9.16, still rising), in line with Eaton and nVent. My reconciled fair value is ~$258 (24.5x a ~$10.5 horizon NTM EPS), only ~6% upside with a 66%-vol distribution, and I keep the forecasters' mean ladder apart from a slightly fatter far-right tail. The second round settled two points. The Texas permit halt also covers behind-the-meter sites, so it hurts UIG's Texas market rather than helping it. The 100% -> 54% -> 12% capex path is Goldman's own (one note, bullish on 2027 levels, slowing in 2028). An unverified AAII headline suggests a ~7% drop on 9/29; Twelve Data shows only -3.65% on 9/28, and the forecast stays at the $244.04 close.
key_drivers: Earnings keep rising while the multiple falls. FY27 consensus is $9.16 (up from $8.80 in 90 days) and horizon NTM EPS is ~$10.5-10.7. At 24.5x that is ~$258, only ~6% above $244. VRT (26.6x FY27) trades in line with ETN and NVT, not at a premium.

The capex path is Goldman's own and belongs to one sell-side house: +54% to $1.2T in 2027 (above consensus), then only +12% to $1.4T in 2028. The 2028 slowdown is the main reason the horizon multiple should stay near 24-25x rather than re-rate.

Texas permit halt (from 2026-09-21; TCEQ report 2026-10-19; ERCOT audit mid-Dec 2026) covers behind-the-meter and islanded sites, so it delays UIG's on-site-power market in Texas instead of helping it.

Visibility is low. No orders or backlog have been disclosed since Q4 2025 ($15.0B), and ~70% of the 2026 FCF guide is customer-deposit build (10-Q). The late-October Q3 print, where consensus of $1.83 is at the top of the guide, is the next test.
Realized vol is ~66% and beta near 2, so the distribution stays very wide: ~16% chance of <$146 and ~15% chance of >$427.
